sections.html:
No South Carolina county has more residents than Greenville: 525,534 in 2020, with 583,125 estimated for 2025. The county seat is the city of Greenville. Fountain Inn, Greer, Mauldin, Simpsonville and Travelers Rest are the remaining cities, and big unincorporated areas like Taylors, Berea and Wade Hampton sit outside all of them.

The housing is a mix of eras: turn-of-the-century houses, mill villages, postwar subdivisions and brand-new builds. Age drives a buyer's repair estimate, and a Travelers Rest house near the mountains attracts a different crowd than a Mauldin house by the interstate, even though one set of county offices taxes both.

Greenville County wants real property tax paid by January 15. Notices typically mail near the end of October. After the deadline, penalties build in steps under S.C. Code 12-45-180.

DatePenalty added to the bill
January 15None, last day to pay
January 163 percent
February 2Further 7 percent
March 17Further 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost

Penalty relief is rare. The Tax Collector will take charges off only if you can show the county itself made a mistake. Visit the South Building, Suite 1100-S, or phone 864.467.7050. Payment can be made at the counter, by mail or on the web, and most payments show as posted within three to five business days.

The lien rides with the parcel, never with a particular owner. When a house closes with this year's tax still open, the escrow agent takes the amount out of the seller's proceeds.

sections.h2: What a sale does to the assessment
sections.html:
Most sales count as an assessable transfer of interest. Real Property Services then appraises the house again, drops the 15 percent limit on yearly increases, and for a point-of-sale reassessment values it as of December 31 of the transfer year. The buyer's new assessment notice commonly shows up the following year.

The January 1 owner of record gets the bill. If the deed moves after that date, that year's bill lists both the former and the incoming owner, and the next year's bill lists only the new one.

  • A home the owner lives in qualifies for the 4 percent legal residence assessment and a credit that wipes out the school operating tax. The form needs a handwritten original signature and has to be delivered by hand or postmarked by January 15. Online filing is not an option.
  • If the new owner will rent the house out, none of that applies, and the first bill they get can come in far higher than yours.
  • The county sets January 30 as the deadline for the 25 percent exemption on transfers from the year before.

Pass this along to your buyer early. For anything unclear, call Real Property Services at 864.467.7300.

Put any appeal on paper. Your assessment notice prints the cutoff date. If you never got a notice, plan on January 15, shifting to the next working day when it falls on a weekend or holiday. S.C. Code 12-60-2510 gives 90 days after mailing when the notice increased value by $1,000 or more.

  1. Mail a letter of objection that includes the tax map number, why you disagree and the value you think is right. Fax and email do not count, and the postmark settles timeliness.
  2. A certified appraiser looks at each appeal filed on time. The assessor then mails you the outcome.
  3. Unhappy with it? You get 30 days from the decision notice to protest to the County Board of Assessment Appeals.
  4. If the Board rules against you in writing, another 30 days opens for the Administrative Law Judge Division.

The address is Real Property Services, Greenville County Square, Suite 1000. New-construction and other increase notices are often scheduled in late summer or early fall.

March 17 ends the grace and makes the bill delinquent, so the Tax Collector sends an execution notice. Thirty days after that mailing, an unpaid account gets a Notice of Seizure sent certified with restricted delivery.

Seized property goes to public auction at the Greenville Convention Center on Exposition Drive, after a notice runs once a week for three weeks. Bidding opens at the total of delinquent tax, penalties and costs plus the current year's tax.

Redemption stays open for 12 months. The former owner, a grantee, or a creditor holding a mortgage or judgment may pay and take the property back, with interest on the bid at 3 percent for months one to three, 6 percent for months four to six, 9 percent for months seven to nine and 12 percent for months ten to twelve. Without redemption, the winning bidder gets a tax deed passing only whatever interest the county held, with no warranty behind it.

Recording happens at the Register of Deeds in Suite S-2100, Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge. Hours are 8:30 am to 5:00 pm on weekdays, and the staff wants walk-ins by 4:30 pm.

State law, in S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 24, sets the deed fee at $1.85 per $500 of value or fraction of it, split $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. A few transfers escape the fee, such as a deed in lieu of foreclosure to the mortgagee or particular family partnership and trust transfers.

A title or escrow firm typically drafts the deed and deducts the fee from closing money. Sending one in yourself? Add a cover letter listing your phone number, a stamped self-addressed envelope and a check made out to Greenville County.

Back taxes slow a sale but rarely kill it. A workable order of steps:

  1. Phone the Tax Collector at 864.467.7050 for a payoff on your parcel. If March 17 is behind you, ask that it include penalties and the execution cost.
  2. Hand that number to the closing agent, who lists it as a charge at the settlement table.
  3. The agent wires the county from your proceeds and records the new deed. You do not mail a separate check.

Beating the auction is almost always the better path. Escrow retires the debt in one step, and you sidestep both the redemption interest and a tax deed.

When you visit an office, carry the deed or tax map number, your latest bill and photo identification. An inherited house adds one more item: expect the closing agent to want estate paperwork before setting a date.

A cash buyer has no lender, so there is no appraisal queue and no repair list to negotiate. How fast you close depends mainly on the title work and the tax payoff, and you can leave the house as it is.

faqs.q: When are Greenville County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment without penalty is due by January 15. Penalties of 3 percent start January 16, a further 7 percent on February 2, and a further 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost on March 17.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Greenville County house if the taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax stays attached to the property and comes out of your proceeds at closing. A cash sale can close with the balance cleared through escrow.

faqs.q: Who handles assessment appeals in Greenville County?
faqs.a: Real Property Services, Greenville County Square, Suite 1000, phone 864.467.7300. The objection must be written, and the postmark decides if you made the deadline.

faqs.q: Does selling my home raise the next owner's tax bill?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which ends the 15 percent cap and resets value. A buyer who does not live in the house also loses the 4 percent legal residence rate.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a house sold at a tax sale?
faqs.a: Twelve months from the sale date. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying taxes, penalties, costs and the stepped interest on the bid.
